# Móði, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Móði** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Móði is not a god of independent myths. His significance lies entirely in his relationship to Þórr and in what he represents for the future after Ragnarök. He is the angry courage that outlives the old gods. Völuspá prophesies that after Ragnarök, a few gods will survive to people the renewed world: Víðarr, Váli, Baldr, Höðr, and the sons of Þórr, Magni and Móði.  They will inherit Mjölnir and the memory of their father's battles.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Móði
- **ASCII form:** modi
- **Meaning:** "The angry one"
- **Domain of influence:** Wrath, Son of Thor
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** ᛘᚢᚦᛁ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 156 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Móði** to *modi* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ó** — Stress on o: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Móði** lives at [/sites/modi/](/sites/modi/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/modi/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/modi/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/modi/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Móði** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — Wrath embodied; the son who inherits the hammer and the fight.
- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — He survives Ragnarök and inherits Mjöllnir; continuity after the end of everything.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — Through him Þórr's line does not end in the serpent's venom; the bloodline carried forward.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Norse tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Poetic Edda](/texts/poetic-edda/) and [Prose Edda](/texts/prose-edda/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
